summary: Tested Single Super Admin Architecture end-to-end. Backend pytest: 21/23 core tests passing (91% success, excluding skipped) after fixing 2 datetime bugs. Frontend: all key admin flows (login, sidebar navigation, dashboard/users/audit/settings/profile pages, logout, route protection, no site-header on /admin/*) working. Uncovered 1 CRITICAL security bug: brute-force lockout is ineffective behind the k8s ingress because request.client.host rotates between multiple upstream IPs (10.208.151.74 / .75), so no single IP+email key ever accumulates 5 failures — verified with 8 consecutive bad-credential attempts returning 401 with zero 429 lockouts. Also fixed 2 tz-naive/aware datetime bugs that were causing 500s on email-OTP verify and password-reset verify.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout INEFFECTIVE. admin_service.check_lockout keys attempts by `request.client.host + ':' + email`, but behind the Kubernetes ingress the upstream client IP alternates between at least two proxy pods (10.208.151.74 / 10.208.151.75). With N proxies the effective threshold becomes 5*N, and in this environment 8 rapid bad-password attempts still all return 401 (zero 429). This defeats the security control entirely. Fix: derive the identifier from just the email (or normalize IP using X-Forwarded-For after trusting the front proxy). Verified in DB — admin_login_attempts entries alternate between the two IPs.

minor.issue: Newly-minted access token can be identical to the previous one when refresh is called within the same wall-clock second (JWT `exp` has 1-second granularity and no `iat`/`jti`). Not a security issue but surprising for clients; consider adding `iat`/`jti` claims.
`signups_current_month` is computed with `thirty_days_ago.replace(day=1)` — the variable name is misleading (it's actually current-month, not 30-day). Cosmetic naming issue only.

Resend integration is rejecting sends to non-owner addresses (SMTPDataError 550). Password-reset + email-OTP fall back to logging (which the spec allows), but the failure spams backend logs on every request. Consider gating send_email with a feature flag or catching earlier.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix brute-force lockout keying — should not depend on request.client.host alone behind a load balancer. Recommended: key on email only, or on trusted X-Forwarded-For header. See rca_of_the_issue.
LOW: Consider adding `iat`/`jti` to admin JWTs so `refresh` always returns a distinct token even within the same second.
critical_code_review_comments: Lockout logic in admin_service.check_lockout uses request.client.host which is not stable behind ingress — see action items.

verify_email_otp and reset_password compared MongoDB naive datetimes to aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) causing 500s — FIXED in this iteration (admin_service.py line ~318, routes/admin.py line ~222).
In routes/admin.py dashboard_stats: `await db.list_collection_names()` is called on every request just to guard projects lookup. Cache or use try/except for perf.

Setting SMTP password: /settings response strips `password` and adds `password_masked`. Good. But PUT payload accepts arbitrary dict without validating shape per key (branding/smtp/etc.) — malformed writes possible. Consider per-key Pydantic models.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Comprehensive test suite exists at /app/backend/tests/test_admin_super.py covering login, session, 2FA (TOTP+Email OTP with pyotp), forgot/reset, audit log, settings (with SMTP password masking check), dashboard, users, and regression on regular /api/auth/login. Frontend admin pages have data-testid conventions: admin-login-page, admin-login-email, admin-login-password, admin-login-submit, admin-nav-{dashboard|users|audit|settings|profile}, admin-logout-btn, admin-layout. NOTE the audit-log nav testid is `admin-nav-audit` (NOT `admin-nav-audit-log`).

rca_of_the_issue.bug: Admin login brute-force lockout does not trigger.
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: curl -X POST https://.../api/admin/auth/login -d '{"email":"x@x","password":"bad"}' 8 times in a row — all return 401, none return 429.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: admin_service.check_lockout counts entries where identifier == '{ip}:{email}'. request.client.host is the immediate upstream connection IP, which in this cluster is one of at least two ingress-proxy pod IPs (10.208.151.74 and 10.208.151.75). Verified in Mongo: admin_login_attempts contains alternating identifiers for the same failing email, so no key ever reaches 5.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Either (a) use email as the identifier (`key = payload.email.lower()`), or (b) parse X-Forwarded-For (`(request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') or '').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host`). Option (a) is simpler and matches the single-admin threat model; option (b) preserves per-IP protection but must trust the proxy.
